title: When the Protocol Burns Anew
premise: Petra Fairweather investigates impossible accidents across the Silence, the gulf between human colonies that severed contact after the Protocol War. When a name from her own buried past appears on the manifest of a ship that never launched, she traces it to a derelict cryo-ark holding two half-populations: one frozen by a court that never had jurisdiction, one by families who paid to flee. As the jump window to a habitable world closes, Petra must choose which half wakes — and discovers the 'impossible accident' was sabotage meant to bury the ark's evidence of who really started the war. She wakes neither half intact but both halves heard, broadcasting the truth system-wide and forging a found crew from strangers on both sides before the window seals.
about_author: E. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years reconstructing disasters no one wanted explained. They write science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people who fall through institutional cracks.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Investigating a cargo skiff's impossible decompression, Petra cross-references manifests and finds her own childhood name — Petra Fairweather, age six — listed on the Meridian Dawn, a colony ship officially never built. The beat is cold unease curdling into recognition: someone has been keeping records of her.

chapters.title: Routes No One Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Petra. She pulls favors along the long haul routes, meeting smugglers and station archivists who form her reluctant found family: gruff pilot Okafor, archivist Junie, ex-medic Brannoc. Each confirms fragments of the Meridian Dawn. Emotional beat: belonging offered cautiously, in fuel debts and shared meals.

chapters.title: What the Court Buried
chapters.summary: POV Junie. Junie decrypts sealed war-era records revealing the Meridian Dawn carried two cryo-banks: convicts sentenced to sleep without trial, and paying refugees. Both were declared lost. Beat: righteous anger; justice was never served, only filed away.

chapters.title: Impossible Accident, Repeated
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Someone sabotages Okafor's ship with the same signature as the skiff case. Petra realizes the pattern she's famous for spotting is aimed at her. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance as the crew chooses to keep flying together rather than scatter.

chapters.title: The Ark Between Worlds
chapters.summary: POV Brannoc. Following a dead beacon, they find the Meridian Dawn adrift, cryo-systems failing on a countdown tied to a jump-window alignment. Brannoc, haunted by patients he couldn't save, must triage which banks can be revived at all. Beat: dread and tenderness in equal measure.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity, Sleeping
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Aboard the ark, Petra finds logs proving the 'accident' that stranded it was sabotage by the tribunal that sentenced the first bank — erasing witnesses to the war's true origin. Her own family were among the payers who fled. Beat: betrayal; her whole career was an escape from this choice.

chapters.title: Wake Orders
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. A tribunal remnant arrives demanding the ark be scuttled. Okafor, once military, recognizes their commander and stalls with a bluff while the crew races to rig revival capacity for one bank only. Beat: loyalty tested; Okafor sacrifices his clean record to buy hours.

chapters.title: The Window Closes
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Climax. With minutes left, Petra refuses the binary: she wakes a mixed first wave — the wrongly convicted alongside volunteer refugees — and hijacks the ark's transmitter to broadcast the tribunal's own sealed confession on every channel. Beat: fury transmuted into justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Waking
chapters.summary: POV Junie. The broadcast fractures the Silence; colonies that stopped speaking begin answering each other through the testimony. The tribunal remnant stands down as its own crews defect. Beat: fragile, disbelieving hope — the found family realizes they've become something larger.

chapters.title: When the Protocol Burns Anew
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Epilogue. The awakened colonists vote to burn the old Protocol and draft a new covenant, with Petra's crew as unlikely signatories. Petra finally reads the manifest line with her name and lets it go. Beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; the long route now has company.
